//: parallelizeTestCollections was true, and it made this suite report failures that depended
on what else happened to be running. Measured on the model-family regression filter:
32 failed / 1245 passed with it on, 0 failed / 1277 passed with it off, and every one of
the six failing families passed 22/22 when run on its own. Different runs failed different
subsets, which is why the suite also looked flaky.
The cause is not in this repository. TensorArena.Create activates an arena per thread, but
arenas pool their backing arrays into a CROSS-ARENA persistent pool on Dispose, and that
pool is shared process-wide. Tests holding arenas on different threads therefore hand each
other arrays. TensorArena lives in the AiDotNet.Tensors package, so the thread-safety fix
belongs there; until it lands, running these collections concurrently is simply not valid.
The cost is close to zero: the same filter takes 10m0s serially against 9m36s in parallel,
because these tests are compute-bound and already saturate the machine.
